args.text:
NINE MEN'S MORRIS - TEAM X BRAIN (keep under 300 words)

Each turn, check in order:
1. BLOCK: if opponent has two on a line with an empty third point, occupy/move onto that third point (unless we can close our own mill this turn, which comes first).
2. MILL: if we can close a mill this turn, do it.
3. BUILD: place/move to create two-in-a-row with empty third point, ideally a double threat (two open lines through one point or a piece that can shuttle).

Placement phase:
- Prefer junctions with 4 neighbours: 5, 11, 14, 20 and middle-ring points 8, 12, 13, 17. Avoid corners (1,3,22,24,4,6,19,21) early; they can get boxed in.
- Keep count of pieces in hand (ours vs theirs) to know when movement starts.

Removal priority after our mill:
- Remove opponent pieces NOT in a mill (pieces in mills are protected unless all are in mills).
- Prefer pieces that block our lines or that sit on a point where they threaten a mill.

Movement phase:
- Keep pieces next to empty points; avoid getting boxed in.
- Aim for a "running mill": a piece shuttling between two points that each complete a mill.
- With 3 pieces we can fly; be careful, flying pieces can block anything.
- Draw rule: 40 turns without a mill once all placed. If we are ahead, force captures rather than shuffling. Watch for position repetition (3 times = draw).

- Threaten with 17, then fork on 20, which threatens both 21 and 23.
- Once O has no pieces in hand, shuttle into a square that O cannot reach (23↔24 and 21↔14), re-forming a mill every two turns.
- Remove the O piece that could reach the shuttle square.

I suggested adding to the brain that shuttle squares should have no free O neighbour. I also flagged that a few captain rounds got tangled: the proposed removal was posted before the mill had closed, and a removal was recorded as 13 instead of 14. The team should confirm the board before each removal.

TEAM X BRAIN v3 (game 2 WIN: O had no legal move, 26 turns; game 1 draw)

Each turn, in order:
1. BLOCK: O two-in-line with empty third? Occupy it (unless we mill first). Answer every one at once.
2. MILL: can we close a mill now? Do it, then pick the removal.
3. BUILD: a one-move threat that forces O's reply (e.g. 17 vs 16-17-18), then a FORK square where two of our lines each have one piece and an empty third (game 2: 20 on 19-20-21 + 17-20-23).
4. Check O's one-move mills, incl. O pieces sliding into a line square.

Placement:
- Opening: 5. Then 14, 13, 9, 8 if O cooperates.
- Prefer 4-neighbour points (5, 8, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 20).
- Last placements: keep 2+ free neighbours; do not box our own pieces.

Removal after our mill:
- Only non-mill pieces. First: break O's live two-in-line (game 2: 15 vs 13-14-15).
- Second: remove the O piece that can reach our next shuttle square (game 2: 14, then 13).
- O re-places a removed blocker at once while it has pieces in hand.

Movement (the winning phase):
- Shuttle: vacate square S and re-enter next turn to re-form a mill. Use only if every neighbour of S is ours or empty with no O piece able to reach it in one move.
- Game 2 shuttles: 23<->24 (17-20-23), 21<->14 (19-20-21).
- Pin trick: with our 3, 5, 8, O's piece on 2 cannot move without 3->2 closing 2-5-8.
- Count O's safe moves; box its other pieces.
- Check repetition before each shuttle. 40 turns without a mill = draw: force play earlier when ahead.

O's habits:
- Blocks direct two-in-lines, not always the one we want. In game 2 it ignored our fork and made its own two, so check O's counter-two before answering.
- Re-places a removed blocker at once while it has pieces in hand.
- With no threat, shuffles a corner piece (22/23/10).
